sub: Our intensive outpatient program by encrypted video, from anywhere in California. It's run by the team at our [rehabilitation center in Los Angeles](/rehabilitation-center).

hero.alt: The reading lounge at Golden State Rehab, with tall bookshelves and two cream armchairs
hero.caption: The reading lounge at our Westwood clinic

sections.a: It's our intensive outpatient program, or IOP, delivered by video. You join live 3-hour sessions, 3 to 5 days a week, in the morning or the evening. That's about 9 to 15 hours of treatment a week, with the curriculum we use in person, and you never have to leave home.

sections.q: Is telehealth rehab right for me?
sections.a: It tends to suit people who live far from Westwood or can't manage the commute. Some people just feel calmer starting treatment from home, and that's a fine reason too. Your free assessment tells you if online IOP is the right level.

items: You live outside the Los Angeles area
You don't have a car or a ride several days a week
You're a parent or caregiver who can't leave the house for hours
You want discreet, flexible scheduling around work
You feel more at ease in your own space

sections.q: Do I have to live in Los Angeles to join?
sections.a: No. Telehealth IOP is open anywhere in California. Our clinic is in Westwood, and we treat online clients across the Westside, from Santa Monica and Brentwood to Beverly Hills and Culver City, and all over the rest of the state.

sections.q: How do I get started with telehealth?
sections.a: It starts with one phone call. Most people begin within days, and there's no waiting list. You'll need a phone or computer with a camera and a private space. We send the link, so there's nothing to download.

items.d: Reach admissions at (424) 208-3120, day or night, or fill out the short form online.

sections.q: What does a week of online IOP look like?
sections.a: It follows the in-person IOP schedule, set at your free assessment and adjusted as you go. Most of your hours are live video groups. Each week you also get a private video session with your primary therapist, plus psychiatry when your treatment plan calls for it.

rows: CBT, DBT, relapse prevention or an open process group, 3 hours each.
A private session for the things you'd rather not say infront of the group.
Our board-certified psychiatrist handles medication by video.
Log in before the day fills up, or log off work and log into group.
Your team lines up ongoing care and alumni support for when you finish.

sections.a: The clinical team that treats people in person at our DHCS-certified clinic, 1964 Westwood Blvd. If you live nearby, you can switch to in-person IOP at any point, since the curriculum is the same.
sections.note: Online IOP is also a common choice for alcohol addiction treatment when the commute is what's in the way.

sections.q: Does insurance pay for telehealth rehab?
sections.a: It depends on your plan. We work with most major PPO plans, and many plans may cover telehealth IOP when it's medically necessary. Admissions calls your insurer for you and explains your benefits before your first session. The check doesn't commit you to anything.
sections.note: Federal parity law and California's SB 855 require plans to cover medically necessary mental health and addiction care.

items: Whether your plan pays for care by video

sections.a: Yes. Sessions run on a HIPAA-compliant video platform, and 42 CFR Part 2 gives addiction records extra federal protection. We never contact your employer. Your information only goes out with your written consent, apart from rare cases the law requires.
sections.note: Taking leave is an option too. FMLA and California's CFRA usually protect your job. [How FMLA works](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla)
